core_principles.text: During the walking forward lunge, the hamstring undergoes a short period of eccentric contraction at the beginning of the stance phase, characterized by elongation of the muscle preceded by high EMG activity.
During the jumping forward lunge, the hamstring muscle length remains almost constant at the first peak, indicating an isometric contraction, followed by a concentric contraction during push-off.
The jumping forward lunge features a pronounced second peak of hamstring activity due to fast hip extension in the push-off phase.
Both walking and jumping forward lunges produce a burst of rectus femoris EMG activity immediately following foot-strike.

During the first part of the stance in the jumping forward lunge, the rectus femoris undergoes an eccentric contraction (muscle lengthening preceded by a peak in activity), followed by a gradual concentric contraction, and ends with an eccentric contraction just before push-off.
For both walking and jumping forward lunges, the gastrocnemius exhibits an initial small burst of EMG activity at foot strike, coinciding with a rapid decrease in muscle length.

specific_findings.text: The walking forward lunge group improved concentric hamstring strength by 35% after six weeks of training, from 92 Nm to 124 Nm (p<0.001).
The walking forward lunge group showed a significant increase in hamstring strength at day two compared to baseline, reaching a mean strength of 107 Nm (p<0.01).

Immediately after the first training session, quadriceps strength decreased from 171 to 162 Nm (p<0.05) in the walking forward lunge group, and from 150 to 132 Nm (p<0.001) in the jumping forward lunge group.
At two days post-exercise, the jumping forward lunge group still had a significant decrease in quadriceps strength compared to baseline, with a mean of 133 Nm (p<0.05).
The jumping forward lunge group showed a significant 2% increase in 30-meter sprint performance compared to baseline after six weeks of training (p<0.001).
The walking forward lunge group improved mean one-leg hop performance from 198 to 212 cm (p<0.001) after six weeks, while the jumping forward lunge group improved from 191 to 205 cm (p<0.01).

Overall muscle pain measured by VAS during the one-leg jump test increased from a median of 0 to 1 in the walking forward lunge group immediately after exercise, and from 0 to 3.5 in the jumping forward lunge group.
After two days, the median VAS pain score was 1 (range 0-6) for the walking forward lunge group and 3.5 (range 0-7) for the jumping forward lunge group.

source: data\lunge\Muscle injury and pain  effects of eccentric exercise, sprint running, forward lunge and sports massage.pdf [part 16/33]

core_principles.text: The quadriceps work eccentrically during the first part of a forward lunge, particularly during the jumping forward lunge variation.
The hamstrings undergo an isometric contraction during the initial period of the stance phase of a forward lunge.
The gastrocnemius works eccentrically during most of the stance phase of a forward lunge.
The length of the hamstrings depends on both the knee and hip angles, with the hip angle having a greater impact on hamstring length than the knee angle.

common_mistakes.text: Believing that the forward lunge elicits prolonged eccentric hamstring activity, whereas it actually undergoes an isometric contraction during the initial stance phase.

specific_findings.text: A training study of twenty-eight junior football players over six weeks compared walking forward lunges and jumping forward lunges, finding no significant differences in performance or pain parameters.
The gastrocnemius muscle shows two distinct EMG peaks during the lunge stance phase: one in the middle representing an eccentric contraction and one at the end.

source: data\lunge\Muscle injury and pain  effects of eccentric exercise, sprint running, forward lunge and sports massage.pdf [part 21/33]

core_principles.text: The quadriceps works eccentrically during the first part of a forward lunge, and this eccentric demand is especially pronounced during a jumping lunge.
The hamstrings perform an isometric contraction during the stance phase of a forward lunge.
The gastrocnemius works eccentrically during a portion of the stance phase of a forward lunge.
Immediately after foot strike during a lunge, eccentric muscle activity occurs primarily in the quadriceps on the front of the thigh, as well as in the hamstrings on the back of the thigh.

specific_findings.text: A six-week training period of walking lunges performed twice a week (evaluated in a study of 32 soccer players) improved hamstring concentric strength, whereas training with jumping lunges improved sprint running performance.

source: data\lunge\Muscle injury and pain  effects of eccentric exercise, sprint running, forward lunge and sports massage.pdf [part 25/33]
